behavior: Remove pre-v3-only readers and ordinary transition names while preserving immutable v3 contracts and local data.
scope: D0 application/domain namespace, atomic encrypted-v3 bootstrap and deterministic Workbench policy checks; no broad qualification or release operations.
delivered: Removed unused pre-v3 compatibility classification types/function/re-export and the unsupported upgrade claim tests. Supported validation uses the existing parser directly.
Renamed ordinary application v3_source_governance and v3_foundation modules, files/test paths and current application/native callers to source_governance/foundation without aliases.
Added responsibility headers to moved/changed owned files; source policy review date remains exactly2026-07-19T00:00:00Z.

Removed automatic plaintext-primary conversion. Existing encrypted stores require supported v3 metadata and successful migration-11 checksum before writer configuration; ambiguous, inconsistent, plaintext and future stores are refused without changing primary/WAL bytes.

Fresh encrypted stores migrate in a private same-volume stage, checkpoint, close and sync before no-clobber publication. Failed/interrupted initialization does not publish an ambiguous primary. Missing-primary recovery artifacts prevent empty recreation.

Windows publication uses no-clobber WRITE_THROUGH without cross-volume copying; prior overwrite callers retain their same-directory contract. Attribute normalization precedes rename; successful publication disables temporary cleanup without accessing the removed source path.
Read-only probes await connection closure and preserve original refusal errors. Pre-v3 migration fixtures were replaced with supported-v3 and synthetic-next-migration failure/retry cases.

Renamed 27 ordinary domain modules/test files and three child directories through 129 Rust files, including evaluation/runtime symbols. Comparison found 419 authorized identifier replacements and 6001 byte-identical literals, with no fixture or migration changes.

Workbench action authorization now accepts an explicit private date seam, while public entry points retain the real clock. Tests use a fixed reviewed date and prove expired policy refuses writes; production policy review date remains unchanged and currently requires real refresh.
immutable_boundaries: SchemaId serialized strings and retained parser/validation code match the prior source exactly.
No SQLx migration bytes, signed keys/signing domains, export record names, backend IDs or format versions changed.
Screening-pattern support, listed-pay/geography projections, secure-storage names and other current-v3 dependencies remain; legacy wording alone is not removal authority.
